title: Recover a set-valued topos point from sheafified representables
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For $U\in\mathcal C$ let $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,U)$, let $h_U^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and put $u(U)=p^{-1}(h_U^\#)$. Then $u$ preserves finite limits, and for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ the maps $u(U_i)\to u(U)$ are jointly surjective. Let $\mathcal N_u$ have objects $(U,a)$ with $a\in u(U)$ and arrows $f:(U,a)\to(V,b)$ given by arrows $f:U\to V$ satisfying $u(f)(a)=b$. This category is small and cofiltered. For every sheaf of sets $F$ the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{(U,a)\in\mathcal N_u^{\mathrm{op}}} F(U)\longrightarrow p^{-1}F,$$
sending a section $t:h_U^\#\to F$ at $(U,a)$ to $p^{-1}(t)(a)$, is a bijection natural in $F$. Colimits and cofilteredness use [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: Write $L(U)=p^{-1}(h_U^\#)=u(U)$. The covariant representable $U\mapsto h_U$ preserves finite limits, since maps into a limit are compatible families; sheafification preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], and $p^{-1}$ preserves them by [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Thus $L$ preserves the terminal object, products, and equalizers. Since $\mathcal C$ is small in the universe fixed by [def-weil-size-convention], the disjoint union of the sets $L(U)$ and the corresponding arrow sets is small, so $\mathcal N_u$ is small. The terminal object gives a pointed object; for $(U,a)$ and $(V,b)$, the element $(a,b)$ in $L(U\times V)$ maps to both. For parallel arrows $(U,a)\rightrightarrows(V,b)$, preservation of their equalizer supplies a pointed equalizing object. These are exactly the nonemptiness, common-source, and equalization conditions for cofilteredness.

proof.text:
For a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$, write $j_i:h_{U_i}^{\#}\to h_U^{\#}$. We prove joint epimorphy by cancellation. Let $r,s:h_U^{\#}\to H$ be maps to a sheaf with $rj_i=sj_i$ for all $i$. For $t\in h_U^{\#}(T)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives a covering $\{T_a\to T\}$ on which $t$ is represented by arrows $g_a:T_a\to U$. Pullback and composition of coverings in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] give a covering $\{T_a\times_U U_i\to T\}$. On each member, the restricted section $t$ is the image under $j_i$ of the section represented by the projection to $U_i$. Thus naturality and $rj_i=sj_i$ make $r_T(t)$ and $s_T(t)$ equal on that covering. The equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $H(T)\to\prod_{a,i}H(T_a\times_U U_i)$ injective, so $r_T(t)=s_T(t)$ and hence $r=s$.
For any set $E$, the natural adjunction in [def-trf-geometric-morphism] carries maps $v,w:L(U)\to E$ agreeing after all $L(U_i)\to L(U)$ to maps $r,s:h_U^{\#}\to p_*E$ agreeing after all $j_i$. The cancellation just proved implies $v=w$. If some $x\in L(U)$ were outside the union of these images, the constant-zero map and the characteristic function of $\{x\}$ from $L(U)$ to $\{0,1\}$ would agree on every image but differ at $x$, a contradiction. Therefore the maps $u(U_i)\to u(U)$ are jointly surjective.

proof.text:
For a set $E$, the sheaf $p_*E$ satisfies, naturally in $U$, 
$$(p_*E)(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_U^\#,p_*E)\cong\operatorname{Map}(p^{-1}h_U^\#,E)=\operatorname{Map}(L(U),E).$$
The first bijection is Yoneda after sheafification, using [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection]; the second is the adjunction in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Naturality in an arrow $f:U\to V$ is precomposition with $L(f)$, by the naturality clause of [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection].

For a sheaf of sets $F$, set $S(F)=\varinjlim_{(U,a)\in\mathcal N_u^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U)$. By the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], a map $S(F)\to E$ is a family of maps $\phi_{U,a}:F(U)\to E$ compatible with every pointed arrow. Currying gives $\tau_U(s)(a)=\phi_{U,a}(s)$; compatibility is exactly naturality of $\tau:F\to p_*E$ under the identification of Step 3. Hence
$$\operatorname{Map}(S(F),E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,p_*E)\cong\operatorname{Map}(p^{-1}F,E),$$
naturally in $E$. By the Yoneda uniqueness of representing objects this yields a natural bijection $S(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}F$. Tracing the construction, the bijection sends the class of $s\in F(U)$ at $a\in L(U)$ to $p^{-1}(s)(a)$, exactly the displayed canonical map; postcomposition with a morphism of sheaves $F\to G$ preserves this formula, so the bijection is natural in $F$.

lean.statement: theorem site_point_reconstruction_sets {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) [HasFiniteLimits C] [HasWeakSheafify J.toGrothendieck (Type v)] (p : GeometricMorphism (Type v) (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type v))) : PreservesFiniteLimits (sitePointFunctor J p) ∧ (∀ (I : Type (max u v)) (U : C) (Ui : I → C) (f : ∀ i, Ui i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows Ui f ∈ J U → ∀ x : (sitePointFunctor J p).obj U, ∃ (i : I) (y : (sitePointFunctor J p).obj (Ui i)), (sitePointFunctor J p).map (f i) y = x) ∧ IsCofiltered (sitePointNeighbourhood J p) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type v)), ∃ (c : Cocone (sitePointSectionDiagram J p F)) (e : c.pt ≅ p.inverse.obj F), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ (∀ (U : C) (a : (sitePointFunctor J p).obj U) (s : F.obj.obj (op U)), e.hom (c.ι.app (Opposite.op ⟨U, a⟩) s) = (p.inverse.map (sitePointSectionHom J F s)) a)) ∧ (∀ (F G : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type v)) (α : F ⟶ G) (U : C) (s : F.obj.obj (op U)), sitePointSectionHom J G ((Sheaf.homEquiv α).app (op U) s) = sitePointSectionHom J F s ≫ α)
